findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the exact predicate the loop uses for 'not inline-runnable' (e.g. eval_solver.INLINE_UNADMISSIBLE_CRITERIA, currently {ISF}) and separate the container class, which is inline-runnable (pass1_container) but currently blocked by 'container-material-unrecoverable' — stating whether containers are quarantined for that distinct reason or excluded from scope entirely.
evidence: Plan: 'the container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) and the ISF class — is quarantined immediately on first encounter with the same ticket, reason "finder not inline-runnable"'
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:32 `INLINE_UNADMISSIBLE_CRITERIA = frozenset({"ISF"})`

src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:30-31 'Container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) ARE admissible — they run over a (parent, children, roster) decomposition — so they are deliberately NOT listed here.'

src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_admission.py:132-156 skips container criteria under a DISTINCT reason 'container-material-unrecoverable' (a temporary sidecar-corpus limitation), not because the finder cannot run on inline text
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:120-130 `_run_criterion_case` runs container criteria via `passes.pass1_container` — they are runnable
findings.finding: Quarantine trigger #2 bundles the container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) into the 'not inline-runnable' class with reason 'finder not inline-runnable', but the codebase defines that class authoritatively as INLINE_UNADMISSIBLE_CRITERIA = frozenset({'ISF'}) and states container criteria are deliberately excluded because they ARE admissible; the plan never states the predicate the loop uses to decide inline-runnability, so the referenced class vocabulary is mis-defined and under-specified.
findings.location: Approach → Quarantine breaker, trigger 2 ("Not inline-runnable (container/ISF-class)") + AC line 'A container/ISF-class criterion (finder not inline-runnable) is quarantined on FIRST encounter'
scenarios: An executor resolves 'finder not inline-runnable' to the existing INLINE_UNADMISSIBLE_CRITERIA set and never quarantines G3/G4/decomp-shape, contradicting the AC that asserts a container criterion is quarantined on first encounter
The loop permanently quarantines decomp-shape (an admissible criterion) and files an unreliable ticket that will never resolve, defeating the gap-only convergence goal
findings.suggested_fix: Split trigger #2 into (a) truly-not-inline-runnable = eval_solver.INLINE_UNADMISSIBLE_CRITERIA (ISF), quarantined with reason 'finder not inline-runnable'; and (b) container criteria (CONTAINER_CRITERIA = G3/G4/decomp-shape), which are admissible in principle but blocked by the corpus lacking per-child material ('container-material-unrecoverable') — either give them their own reason string or declare them out of the loop's gap scope. Correct the AC accordingly (e.g. seed an ISF-class criterion, not a container one, for the first-encounter test).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow quarantine trigger #2 to the criteria the codebase actually rejects inline (`INLINE_UNADMISSIBLE_CRITERIA`, currently just ISF) and stop quarantining container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape), which eval_solver.py:30-31 marks admissible via the children-payload runner path.
evidence: Plan: 'the container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) and the ISF class — is quarantined immediately on first encounter ... reason "finder not inline-runnable"'
eval_solver.py:26-32: 'Container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) ARE admissible — they run over a (parent, children, roster) decomposition — so they are deliberately NOT listed here'
eval_solver.py:32: `INLINE_UNADMISSIBLE_CRITERIA = frozenset({"ISF"})` — only ISF, not the container criteria
The parent epic's prose asserts the same container grouping the code contradicts, so the plan copies a stale framing rather than the machinery's actual contract (cargo-cult)
findings.finding: Quarantine trigger #2 treats container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) as 'not inline-runnable' and quarantines them on first encounter, but the codebase deliberately classifies only ISF as inline-unadmissible; containers ARE runnable.
findings.location: Approach > Quarantine breaker, trigger 2 ('Not inline-runnable (container/ISF-class)'); AC line 'A container/ISF-class criterion (finder not inline-runnable) is quarantined on FIRST encounter'
scenarios: A run encounters G3/G4/decomp-shape with no fixture and files an unreliable-criterion ticket for them, when the admission machinery would actually mine them via the children-payload runner path
The AC's 'seeded such criterion' test would pass against ISF but codify the wrong contract for containers
findings.suggested_fix: Key the first-encounter quarantine off `rebar.llm.evals.eval_solver.INLINE_UNADMISSIBLE_CRITERIA` (a frozenset the runner already consults) rather than a hardcoded 'container/ISF-class' grouping, so the loop quarantines exactly what the finder rejects and leaves container criteria for the admission runner to mine over their decomposition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add acceptance criteria that exercise the transient-error retry path and the BudgetExceeded fatal-stop-with-reconcile-and-resume path against the stubbed runner.
evidence: 'A transient model/transport error in an admission attempt is RETRYABLE and retried within the run.'
'BudgetExceeded is FATAL and non-retryable: the run stops with completed criteria admitted and their spend reconciled, and the next interval resumes.'
The only budget-related AC asserts the pre-flight estimate stop with cap_usd=25.0, not the mid-admission BudgetExceeded fatal-stop-and-reconcile.
findings.finding: The Failure-disposition section describes two behaviors that no acceptance criterion exercises: (a) a transient model/transport error is 'RETRYABLE and retried within the run', and (b) 'BudgetExceeded is FATAL and non-retryable: the run stops with completed criteria admitted and their spend reconciled, and the next interval resumes.' The ledger AC tests only the pre-flight headroom stop, which is a distinct path from a BudgetExceeded raised mid-admission.
findings.location: Approach → Failure disposition; Acceptance Criteria (ledger AC)
scenarios: A mid-admission BudgetExceeded leaves spend un-reconciled or fails to resume next interval, and no test would catch it.
The retry-on-transient path regresses to non-retry with no failing test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add ACs: (1) a stubbed runner raising a transient error once is retried and the criterion still admits; (2) a stubbed runner raising BudgetExceeded stops the run with already-admitted criteria persisted and reconciled and no counter increment for the interrupted criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Co-locate each failure signal with its emitting sub-step: state that `skipped-unbalanced` is read from FixtureEmitReport.skipped_unbalanced (emit step) and 'candidates fail to reproduce' is read from the admission runner's drift/withheld result (admission step), so the counter increment reads both.
evidence: Plan: 'A run is a failure for a criterion when its emitted spec's candidates fail to reproduce, OR when the criterion is reported `skipped-unbalanced`'
src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_emit.py:33 `skipped_unbalanced: list[str]` is a field on FixtureEmitReport returned by emit_specs — an EMIT-time signal
Reproduction failure is an ADMISSION-time signal (fixture_admission drift entries), a separate report object from the emit report
findings.finding: The consecutive-failure counter is fed by two signals emitted by two different sub-steps — the emitter's FixtureEmitReport.skipped_unbalanced field and the admission runner's reproduction-failure result — but the plan does not co-locate which sub-step's report each signal is read from, leaving the increment's source contract ambiguous for the executor.
findings.location: Approach → Quarantine breaker, trigger 1 ("Three consecutive failed runs")
scenarios: An executor wires the counter to only one of the two report objects and silently misses the other failure kind, so the third-run ticket never fires for that kind

findings.checklist_item: Either name the concurrency guard that makes 'no OPEN ticket → file' atomic (e.g. a store-level unique-title constraint or an advisory lock the loop holds across query+create), or soften the claim to reconcile duplicates on read (dedupe the title→unreliable map by picking a canonical ticket id and specify the counter-reset behavior when >1 open ticket exists for a criterion).
evidence: Plan: 'Ticket creation is IDEMPOTENT — the loop files only when no OPEN ticket with that exact title exists — so overlapping runs cannot double-create, and the once-per-interval due-stamp serializes ordinary runs.'
Plan: 'It is also directly invocable as a command, so an operator, a cron, or any CI provider can drive it.'

src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:178-184 — create_ticket returns only an advisory duplicate_warning for a same-normalized-title ticket in the recency window; it does not reject, so title uniqueness is not enforced at the store.
The due-stamp serializes only the operation-driven path ('ordinary runs'); a manual/cron invocation concurrent with an operation-advanced run is a check-then-act window with no lock named.
findings.finding: The idempotent-ticket-creation mechanism is a check-then-act (query OPEN tickets with the exact title, then file only if none) whose 'overlapping runs cannot double-create' claim is not backed by an atomic guarantee; ticket creation enforces no title uniqueness and the loop is explicitly also directly invocable as a command alongside the operation-driven due-stamp path.
findings.location: Approach → 'How the quarantine feeds the selector' and 'Portability' paragraphs
scenarios: An operator invokes the loop command manually at the same interval an operation advances the due-stamp, both query 'no open unreliable-criterion: <id> ticket', both file — two tickets for one criterion.
A CI provider and a cron both wired to the same command fire concurrently on the third-failure boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence in the quarantine-feeds-selector paragraph: the title→unreliable map builder collapses multiple open tickets for one criterion to the earliest-created id, and counter reset requires ALL open tickets for the criterion to be closed; and state whether concurrent invocation is guarded (a held lock / due-stamp claim) or tolerated-then-reconciled, rather than asserting it cannot happen.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the loop determines inline-runnability (e.g. a registry criterion attribute vs an enumerated id set), so the not-inline-runnable trigger is executable without a design choice.
evidence: 'a criterion whose finder cannot run on inline plan text — the container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) and the ISF class — is quarantined immediately'
The plan names the classes but never states how the loop programmatically classifies an arbitrary registry criterion as inline-runnable or not.
findings.finding: The mechanism by which the loop determines a criterion is 'not inline-runnable' (container G3/G4/decomp-shape or ISF class) is not specified — whether via a registry attribute/flag on the criterion, a hardcoded id set, or an introspected finder capability. AC5 seeds 'such a criterion' but does not fix the detection contract.
findings.location: Approach → Quarantine breaker, trigger 2 ('Not inline-runnable (container/ISF-class)') and AC5
scenarios: A new container-class criterion is added to the registry later; the loop must decide inline-runnability from data, but no attribute is named to read.
Executor must choose between a hardcoded id list and a registry flag with no stated default.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the source of truth for inline-runnability (a registry field such as `criterion.inline_runnable`, or an explicit constant id set seeded from the parent epic) and reference it in trigger 2 and AC5.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the consecutive-failure quarantine threshold is configurable (with default 3) or intentionally fixed, matching the treatment of the interval and cap.
evidence: 'On the third such consecutive run the loop files the ticket.'
Interval is 'configurable (default 30 days)' and cap is a parameter, but the threshold 3 has no configurability statement.
findings.finding: The '3 consecutive failed runs' quarantine threshold is stated as a fixed value while the interval (default 30 days) and cap ($25) are explicitly configurable. The plan does not say whether the failure threshold is configurable, so an evolving policy value is effectively hardcoded.
scenarios: Operators want a stricter (2) or looser (5) threshold and must edit code rather than config.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose the threshold as a config value defaulting to 3, alongside the interval and cap.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a doc/ADR (or AGENTS.md update) capturing the self-healing loop, its quarantine-ticket title contract, and the title-vs-selector-reason-string distinction.
evidence: 'Closer to the reconciler's convergence breaker (_config_schema, ADR 0027/0028) ... the sibling a5bf records the pattern.'
No scope/DoD item creates or updates a doc/ADR for the new self-healing loop and quarantine trigger contract.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new persistent self-healing repair loop with a ticket-based quarantine breaker — a new command, new state format, and a new operational pattern — but cites ADRs 0027/0028 only as prior art and does not commit to documenting this new loop/breaker in an ADR, AGENTS.md, or design doc.
scenarios: A future maintainer encounters the quarantine-ticket title contract and unreliable-map wiring with no design record explaining the two-string distinction.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Scope/DoD bullet to record an ADR or design-doc note describing the loop, the exact `unreliable-criterion: <id>` title contract, and how it differs from the selector's `unreliable-criterion:{ticket_id}` reason string.
